subject: AI & Agents
title: Ada Lovelace and the First Algorithm
description: A quick win: understand Ada Lovelace and the First Algorithm.

hook.text: In 1843, a countess wrote what many consider the world's first computer program.

buildup.text: Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine — a mechanical computer.

discovery.text: She wrote detailed notes including an algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers.

twist.text: She also predicted machines could compose music — 100 years before anyone tried.

climax.text: Lovelace saw that machines could manipulate symbols, not just numbers. That insight fuels all of AI.

punchline.text: The first programmer imagined AI before AI existed.

quiz.question: What did Ada Lovelace predict machines could do?

details.summary: In the 1840s, Ada Lovelace wrote what many consider the first computer algorithm for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine. She also foresaw machines might one day compose music and beyond.
details.whyItMatters: Lovelace's work established that machines could be instructed to perform complex operations. Her vision of computing beyond pure calculation foreshadowed the creative potential of modern AI.
takeaways: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for a computing machine
She envisioned machines creating music and art in the 1840s
Her work laid conceptual foundations for computer programming

faq.question: What algorithm did Ada Lovelace write?
faq.answer: She wrote an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers on Babbage's Analytical Engine. Her detailed notes went beyond the calculation itself to envision the broader potential of programmable machines.

faq.question: Why is Ada Lovelace considered important to AI history?
faq.answer: She was the first person to articulate that machines could manipulate symbols beyond pure numbers. This conceptual leap laid the groundwork for modern computing and eventually artificial intelligence.
